Damrong's Simple Teleop¶

Set up¶

This project has been tested on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS.

Please verify that we have a directory named teleop (or any name) that contain these files:

$ ls -RF teleop/
teleop/:
DamrongAsset/  Damrong_teleop.ipynb

teleop/DamrongAsset:
asset/  DamrongAsset_package.xml

teleop/DamrongAsset/asset:
manipuland/  scene/

teleop/DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland:
cuboid.obj  cuboid.sdf  cuboid.stl  cuboid.vtk  peg.obj  peg.sdf  peg.stl  peg.vtk

teleop/DamrongAsset/asset/scene:
Damrong_peg_cuboid.dmd.yaml

Please follow these steps to set up the teleop simulation.

  1. Create a virtual environment in a subdirectory, say venv.
teleop $ mkdir venv
teleop $ python3 -m venv venv
teleop $ source venv/bin/activate

The prompt will have (venv). This is important because we don't want this project to change the existing Python environment on the computer yet.

(venv) teleop $
  1. Install the manipulation package with the nightly Drake build (or any specific version) in the virtual environment. Please be patient. It might download a few gigabytes.
(venv) teleop $ pip install manipulation[all] --extra-index-url https://drake-packages.csail.mit.edu/whl/nightly/
  1. Install the notebook package.
(venv) teleop $ pip install notebook
  1. Run this notebook.
(venv) jupyter notebook

You should see Damrong_teleop.ipynb (a copy of this file) in the list. Open it.

  1. Change DamrongAsset_package_xml in the following cell to the appropriate path.
In [1]:
# Change to where you store the asset files.
DamrongAsset_pacakge_xml = "/home/damrongguoy/project/teleop/DamrongAsset/DamrongAsset_package.xml"

Preliminary: Generate and Verify Assets¶

I started from the given .stl files:

DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/cuboid.stl
DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/peg.stl

I created their compatible assets (.obj, .vtk, .sdf) for the hydroelastic contact model:

DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/cuboid.obj
DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/cuboid.vtk
DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/cuboid.sdf

DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/peg.obj
DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/peg.vtk
DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/peg.sdf

The hydroelastic contact model needs a collision geometry represented as a tetrahedral mesh in a VTK file. The following document explains how to generate an appropriate tetrahedral mesh from a surface mesh in STL or OBJ format.

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VZtVsxIjOLKvgQ8SNSrF6PtWuPW5z9PP7-dQuxfmqpc/edit?usp=sharing

For visual geometry, Drake prefers an OBJ file. The above document also describes one way to convert STL to OBJ.

Verify Inertia Tensor¶

A common problem is the incorrect inertia tensor specified in the description file, which contaminates the solution of the governing equations.

The code below will calculate the inertia matrix from the mesh. It is a simplified and customized version of this snippet in drake/bindings/pydrake/multibody/_mesh_model_maker.py.

Later we will use this calculation to verify the content in the .sdf files.

In [3]:
def CalculateInertiaMatrixFromDamrongMesh(package_path_to_asset_prefix, mass_density):
    package_map = PackageMap()
    package_map.AddPackageXml(DamrongAsset_pacakge_xml)
    obj_path = package_map.ResolveUrl(package_path_to_asset_prefix+".obj")
    
    print()
    print(obj_path)
    print(f"Input mass density: {mass_density} kg/m^3")

    # The OBJ file uses millimeters. Convert to meters.
    mesh_scale = 0.001
    surface_mesh = ReadObjToTriangleSurfaceMesh(filename = obj_path, scale = mesh_scale)

    # G = the expressed-in frame of the object.
    mesh_G = surface_mesh
    p_GoMin, p_GoMax = mesh_G.CalcBoundingBox()
    size = p_GoMax - p_GoMin
    print(f"Size of bounding box in meters (scaled mm to m): {size[0]} x {size[1]} x {size[2]} meters")

    # This calculation is relative to the origin of the coordinate
    # frame of the mesh, which may or may not coincide with the
    # center of mass, depending on the shape of the object.
    M_GGo_G = CalcSpatialInertia(mesh = mesh_G, density = mass_density)
    mass = M_GGo_G.get_mass()
    volume = mass / mass_density
    p_GoGcm = M_GGo_G.get_com()
    print(f"Mass: {mass} kg")
    print(f"Volume: {volume} cubic meters")
    print(f"Center of mass (p_GoGcm): [{p_GoGcm[0]}, {p_GoGcm[1]}, {p_GoGcm[2]}]")

    # Shift the matrix tensor to the center of mass.
    M_GGcm_G = M_GGo_G.Shift(p_GoGcm)

    # Now we can calculate relative to the center of mass.
    I_GGcm_G = M_GGcm_G.CalcRotationalInertia()
    moments = I_GGcm_G.get_moments()
    products = I_GGcm_G.get_products()
    
    subs = dict()
    p_GoGcm_str = " ".join([str(x) for x in p_GoGcm])
    subs["inertial_pose"] = f"{p_GoGcm_str} 0 0 0"
    subs["mass"] = mass
    subs["ixx"] = moments[0]
    subs["iyy"] = moments[1]
    subs["izz"] = moments[2]
    subs["ixy"] = products[0]
    subs["ixz"] = products[1]
    subs["iyz"] = products[2]
    subs["mesh_scale"] = "{s} {s} {s}".format(s = mesh_scale)
    subs["package_path_to_asset_prefix"] = package_path_to_asset_prefix
    
    _SDF_TEMPLATE = """
          <inertial>
            <pose>{inertial_pose}</pose>
            <mass>{mass}</mass>
            <inertia>
              <ixx>{ixx}</ixx> <ixy>{ixy}</ixy> <ixz>{ixz}</ixz>
              <iyy>{iyy}</iyy> <iyz>{iyz}</iyz>
              <izz>{izz}</izz>
            </inertia>
          </inertial>
          <visual name="visual">
            <geometry>
              <mesh>
                <uri>{package_path_to_asset_prefix}.obj</uri>
                <scale>{mesh_scale}</scale>
              </mesh>
            </geometry>
          </visual>
          <collision name="collision">
            <geometry>
              <mesh>
                <uri>{package_path_to_asset_prefix}.vtk</uri>
                <scale>{mesh_scale}</scale>
              </mesh>
            </geometry>
    """

    print(_SDF_TEMPLATE.format(**subs))
    print("Don't forget mesh scale: <scale>", subs["mesh_scale"], "</scale>")
    print()

Verify the cuboid¶

  • The mass density of water is 1 kg/m^3.
  • The density of iron is 7800 kg/m^3.
  • The density of HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene) plastic is about 950 kg/m^3.
  • The density of PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride) is about 1400 kg/m^3.

For simplicity, we use 950 kg/m^3 (HDPE) for both the cuboid and the peg.

Please make sure the result from CalculateInertiaMatrixFromDamrongMesh() matches the .sdf file.¶

)

def WaitToActivateGamepad():
  count = 0;  
  while(meshcat.GetGamepad().index == None):
    if (count==10):
        break;
    count = count + 1    
    print(
      f"{count}. Press a button on the gamepad with the meshcat window in focus to activate the gamepad."
    )
    time.sleep(3)

WaitToActivateGamepad()
if (meshcat.GetGamepad().index != None):
    print("Thank you! The gamepad is activated.")
else:
    print("Continue without a gamepad. The simulation might quit too early.")

I copied this GamepadDiffIK system from Russ. If it's hard to follow the code, just use it without reading for now.¶

In [8]:
class GamepadDiffIK(LeafSystem):
    def __init__(self, meshcat, plant, frame_E):
        """
        Args:
            meshcat: A Meshcat instance.
            plant: A multibody plant (to use for differential ik). It is
              probably the plant used for control, not for simulation (it should only contain the robot, not the objects).
            frame: A frame in to control `plant`.
        """
        LeafSystem.__init__(self)

        self.DeclareVectorInputPort("robot_state", plant.num_multibody_states())
        self.DeclareInitializationDiscreteUpdateEvent(self.Initialize)

        port = self.DeclareVectorOutputPort(
            "iiwa.position", plant.num_positions(), self.OutputIiwaPosition
        )
        # The gamepad has undeclared state.  For now, we accept it,
        # and simply disable caching on the output port.
        port.disable_caching_by_default()

        port = self.DeclareVectorOutputPort("wsg.position", 1, self.OutputWsgPosition)

        self.DeclareDiscreteState(plant.num_positions())  # iiwa position
        self.DeclareDiscreteState(1)  # wsg position
        self.DeclareDiscreteState(1)  # gripper button pressed
        self._time_step = 0.05
        self.DeclarePeriodicDiscreteUpdateEvent(self._time_step, 0, self.Integrate)

        self._meshcat = meshcat
        self._plant = plant
        self._plant_context = plant.CreateDefaultContext()

        if frame_E is None:
            frame_E = plant.GetFrameByName("body")  # wsg gripper frame
        self._frame_E = frame_E

        params = DifferentialInverseKinematicsParameters(
            plant.num_positions(), plant.num_velocities()
        )
        q0 = plant.GetPositions(plant.CreateDefaultContext())
        params.set_time_step(self._time_step)
        params.set_nominal_joint_position(q0)
        params.set_end_effector_angular_speed_limit(2)
        params.set_end_effector_translational_velocity_limits([-2, -2, -2], [2, 2, 2])
        iiwa14_velocity_limits = np.array([1.4, 1.4, 1.7, 1.3, 2.2, 2.3, 2.3])
        params.set_joint_velocity_limits(
            (-iiwa14_velocity_limits, iiwa14_velocity_limits)
        )
        params.set_joint_centering_gain(10 * np.eye(7))

        self._diff_ik_params = params
        self._wsg_open = 0.107
        self._wsg_close = 0.002

    def Initialize(self, context, discrete_state):
        discrete_state.set_value(
            0,
            self.get_input_port().Eval(context)[: self._plant.num_positions()],
        )
        discrete_state.set_value(1, [self._wsg_open])
        discrete_state.set_value(2, [0])

    def Integrate(self, context, discrete_state):
        gamepad = self._meshcat.GetGamepad()

        # https://beej.us/blog/data/javascript-gamepad/
        def CreateStickDeadzone(x, y):
            stick = np.array([x, y])
            deadzone = 0.3
            m = np.linalg.norm(stick)
            if m < deadzone:
                return np.array([0, 0])
            over = (m - deadzone) / (1 - deadzone)
            return stick * over / m

        left = CreateStickDeadzone(gamepad.axes[0], gamepad.axes[1])
        right = CreateStickDeadzone(gamepad.axes[2], gamepad.axes[3])

        V_WE_desired = np.zeros((6,))
        # TODO(russt): Properly implement rpydot to angular velocity.
        V_WE_desired[0] = -0.2 * right[0]  # Right stick x => wx
        V_WE_desired[1] = 0.2 * right[0]  # Right stick y => wy
        if gamepad.button_values[4] > 0.2 or gamepad.button_values[5] > 0.2:
            # l1/r1 => wz
            V_WE_desired[2] = 0.2 * (
                gamepad.button_values[5] - gamepad.button_values[4]
            )
        V_WE_desired[3] = -0.2 * left[0]  # Left stick x => vx
        V_WE_desired[4] = 0.2 * left[1]  # Left stick y => vy
        if gamepad.button_values[6] > 0.2 or gamepad.button_values[7] > 0.2:
            # l2/r2 => vx
            V_WE_desired[5] = 0.2 * (
                gamepad.button_values[7] - gamepad.button_values[6]
            )

        q = np.copy(context.get_discrete_state(0).get_value())
        self._plant.SetPositions(self._plant_context, q)
        result = DoDifferentialInverseKinematics(
            self._plant,
            self._plant_context,
            V_WE_desired,
            self._frame_E,
            self._diff_ik_params,
        )
        if result.status != DifferentialInverseKinematicsStatus.kNoSolutionFound:
            discrete_state.set_value(0, q + self._time_step * result.joint_velocities)

        # Toggle gripper open/close based on buttons
        x_pressed = context.get_discrete_state(2).get_value()[0]
        if gamepad.button_values[1] > 0.5:
            if not x_pressed:
                wsg_position = context.get_discrete_state(1).get_value()[0]
                if wsg_position == self._wsg_open:
                    discrete_state.set_value(1, [self._wsg_close])
                else:
                    discrete_state.set_value(1, [self._wsg_open])
            discrete_state.set_value(2, [1])
        else:
            discrete_state.set_value(2, [0])

        # TODO(russt): This doesn't actually work yet, since the event status
        # is being discarded in the pybind later.
        if gamepad.button_values[0] > 0.5:
            return EventStatus.ReachedTermination(self, "x button pressed")

        return EventStatus.Succeeded()

    def OutputIiwaPosition(self, context, output):
        output.set_value(context.get_discrete_state(0).get_value())

    def OutputWsgPosition(self, context, output):
        output.set_value(context.get_discrete_state(1).get_value())

Teleop with a gamepad¶

Test gamepad https://gamepad-tester.com/

END EFFECTOR CONTROL
-----------------------------------------
+/- x-axis         - leftjoy left / right
+/- y-axis         - leftjoy up / down
+/- roll           - rightjoy up / down
+/- pitch          - rightjoy left / right
+/- z-axis         - l2 / r2
+/- yaw            - l1 / r1

GRIPPER CONTROL
-----------------------------------------
open / close       - square / circle (O)

-----------------------------------------
x button           - quit

    default_free_body_pose:
        # The peg frame P has its origin at the center of the peg, so
        # setting X_WP with z = 5cm (half length) will place the peg
        # on the World's X-Y plane.
        peg:
            translation: [0, -0.6, 0.05]

    name: nonconvex_cuboid
    file: package://DamrongAsset/asset/manipuland/cuboid.sdf
    default_free_body_pose:
        # The name of this frame "cuboid" has to match what specified in
        # the .sdf file.
        cuboid:
            translation: [-0.15, -0.6, 0.05]
- add_model:
    name: yellow_bell_pepper
    file: package://drake_models/veggies/yellow_bell_pepper_no_stem_low.sdf
    default_free_body_pose:

        yellow_bell_pepper_no_stem:

Define a simple leaf system to report contact results¶

In [11]:
class ContactReporter(LeafSystem):
    def __init__(self, scene_graph_inspector, contact_pair_names):
        super().__init__()  # Don't forget to initialize the base class.

        # Debug
        self.DebugPrintAllGeometryNames(scene_graph_inspector)
        
        self._geometry_id_pairs = [
          [self.FindGeometryId(scene_graph_inspector, pair[0]),
           self.FindGeometryId(scene_graph_inspector, pair[1])]
          for pair in contact_pair_names]

        self.DeclareAbstractInputPort(
            name="contact_results",
            model_value=Value(
                # Input port will take ContactResults from MultibodyPlant
                ContactResults()))

        # Declare as many output ports as the specified contact pairs.
        for pair in contact_pair_names:
          port_name = pair[0]+ "+" + pair[1]
          geometry_pair_ids = [
            self.FindGeometryId(scene_graph_inspector, pair[0]),
            self.FindGeometryId(scene_graph_inspector, pair[1])]
          self.DeclareVectorOutputPort(
            port_name, 6, 
              partial(self.OutputSpatialForce, geometry_pair_ids))
        
        # Calling `ForcedPublish()` will trigger the callback.
        self.DeclareForcedPublishEvent(self.Publish)

    def DebugPrintAllGeometryNames(self, scene_graph_inspector):
        for id in scene_graph_inspector.GetAllGeometryIds():
          print(scene_graph_inspector.GetName(id))  
    
    def FindGeometryId(self, scene_graph_inspector, geometry_name):
        for id in scene_graph_inspector.GetAllGeometryIds():
          if (scene_graph_inspector.GetName(id) == geometry_name):    
            return id
        print(f"ContactReporter::FindGeometryId() cannot find geometry name \"{geometry_name}\"")      
        exit(1)      

    def SelectivePredicate(self, geometry_pair_ids, hydroelastic_contact_info):
        id_M = hydroelastic_contact_info.contact_surface().id_M()
        id_N = hydroelastic_contact_info.contact_surface().id_N()
        return ((id_M == geometry_pair_ids[0] and id_N == geometry_pair_ids[1]) or
                (id_M == geometry_pair_ids[1] and id_N == geometry_pair_ids[0]))
 
    def OutputSpatialForce(self, geometry_pair_ids, context: Context, output: BasicVector) -> None:
        contact_results = self.get_input_port().Eval(context)
        selected_results = contact_results.SelectHydroelastic(
            partial(self.SelectivePredicate, geometry_pair_ids))
        num_selected = selected_results.num_hydroelastic_contacts()
        if (num_selected == 0):
          output.SetFromVector([0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0])
          return  
        if (num_selected == 1):            
          spatial_force = selected_results.hydroelastic_contact_info(0).F_Ac_W()
          output.SetFromVector(spatial_force.get_coeffs())  

    
    def Publish(self, context):
        print()
        print(f"ContactReporter::Publish() called at time={context.get_time()}")
        contact_results = self.get_input_port().Eval(context)
        
        num_hydroelastic_contacts = contact_results.num_hydroelastic_contacts()
        print(f"num_hydroelastic_contacts() = {num_hydroelastic_contacts}")
        
        for c in range(num_hydroelastic_contacts):
            print()
            print(f"hydroelastic_contact_info({c}): {c}-th hydroelastic contact patch")
            hydroelastic_contact_info = contact_results.hydroelastic_contact_info(c)
            
            spatial_force = hydroelastic_contact_info.F_Ac_W()
            print("F_Ac_W(): spatial force (on body A, at centroid of contact surface, in World frame) = ")
            print(f"{spatial_force}")
                        
            print("contact_surface()")
            contact_surface = hydroelastic_contact_info.contact_surface()
            id_M = contact_surface.id_M()
            id_N = contact_surface.id_N()
            print(f"id_M={id_M}, id_N={id_N}")
            num_faces = contact_surface.num_faces()
            total_area = contact_surface.total_area()
            centroid = contact_surface.centroid()
            print(f"total_area(): area of contact surface in m^2 = {total_area}")
            print(f"num_faces(): number of polygons or triangles = {num_faces}")
            print(f"centroid(): centroid (in World frame) = {centroid}")        
        
        print()

Define the system diagram¶

In [12]:
def Damrong_build_diagram():
    builder = DiagramBuilder()

    scenario = LoadScenario(data=scenario_data)
    
    # There's a trade-off between fidelity and speed.
    # If we want fidelity (no strange oscillation), the time_step
    # should be small, like 1 millisecond. If we want speed, the
    # time_step should be larger, like 5 milliseconds.
    #
    # ----------+----------------+-----------
    # time_step | unusually long | real-time
    # (second)  |  oscillation   |   rate
    # ----------+----------------+-----------
    #   1e-3    |      no        |   25%
    #   3e-3    |     rare       |   70%
    #   5e-3    |   sometimes    |  100%
    # ----------+----------------+-----------
    scenario.plant_config.time_step = 3e-3
    station = builder.AddSystem(
        MakeHardwareStation(scenario, meshcat,
                            package_xmls=[DamrongAsset_pacakge_xml]))

    # Set up differential inverse kinematics.
    diff_ik_plant = MakeMultibodyPlant(scenario, model_instance_names=["iiwa"])
    frame = diff_ik_plant.GetFrameByName("iiwa_link_7")
    gamepad = builder.AddSystem(GamepadDiffIK(meshcat, diff_ik_plant, frame))

    builder.Connect(
        gamepad.GetOutputPort("iiwa.position"),
        station.GetInputPort("iiwa.position"),
    )
    builder.Connect(
        gamepad.GetOutputPort("wsg.position"),
        station.GetInputPort("wsg.position"),
    )
    builder.Connect(
        station.GetOutputPort("iiwa.state_estimated"),
        gamepad.GetInputPort("robot_state"),
    )
    
    builder.AddSystem(StopButton(meshcat))

    # Report contact for the finger tip
    contact_reporter = builder.AddSystem(
        ContactReporter(
            station.GetSubsystemByName("scene_graph").model_inspector(),
            contact_outputs))
    builder.Connect(station.GetOutputPort("contact_results"),
                    contact_reporter.get_input_port(0))

    contact_loggers = dict()
    for pair in contact_outputs:
        port_name = pair[0] + "+" + pair[1]
        contact_loggers[port_name] = LogVectorOutput(
            contact_reporter.GetOutputPort(port_name), builder)
    
    station_loggers = dict()
    for out_port in station_outputs:
      station_loggers[out_port] = LogVectorOutput(
          station.GetOutputPort(out_port), builder)
    
    control_loggers = dict()
    for out_port in control_outputs:
        control_loggers[out_port] = LogVectorOutput(
            gamepad.GetOutputPort(out_port), builder)

    diagram = builder.Build()
    # # This one shows the diagram in the output cell of this notebook.
    # RenderDiagram(diagram, max_depth=1)

    # This code block is for debugging by inspecting the system diagram.
    # After generating the .dot files, convert and display them by:
    #    $ dot -Tpng in.dot -o out.png
    #    $ eog out.png
    # dot_code = diagram.GetGraphvizString(max_depth=1)
    # with open("Damrong_teleop_diagram_depth1.dot", "w") as f:
    #     f.write(dot_code)

    return diagram, station_loggers, control_loggers, contact_loggers

Run the teleop simulation¶

In [13]:
def Damrong_teleop_3d():
    if meshcat.GetGamepad().index == None:
        print(
            "Press a button on the gamepad with the meshcat window in focus to activate gamepad support (then run this cell again)."
        )
        return        
    meshcat.ResetRenderMode()
    meshcat.DeleteAddedControls()

    diagram, station_loggers, control_loggers, contact_loggers = Damrong_build_diagram()
    
    simulator = Simulator(diagram)
    simulator.get_mutable_context()

    simulator.set_target_realtime_rate(1.0)
    simulator.AdvanceTo(np.inf)

    # Forced publish after the simulation has finished.
    diagram.ForcedPublish(simulator.get_context())
    
    station_logs = dict()
    for name in station_outputs:
      station_logs[name] = station_loggers[name].FindLog(simulator.get_context())

    control_logs = dict()
    for name in control_outputs:
      control_logs[name] = control_loggers[name].FindLog(simulator.get_context())

    contact_logs = dict()
    for pair in contact_outputs:
      name = pair[0] + "+" + pair[1]
      contact_logs[name] = contact_loggers[name].FindLog(simulator.get_context())

    return station_logs, control_logs, contact_logs

meshcat.StartRecording()
station_logs, control_logs, contact_logs = Damrong_teleop_3d()
meshcat.StopRecording()
meshcat.PublishRecording()

print("\nDone. T H A N K   Y O U !")

Plot controller command (position of the arm and the gripper)¶

In [14]:
def PlotState(state_name, logs, range_components = []):
  title = state_name + " vs Time"  
  log = logs[state_name]
  times = log.sample_times()
  if range_components == []:  
    range_components = range(0, len(log.data()))

  plt.figure(figsize=(10,4))

  for i in range_components:  
    data = log.data()[i]  
    plt.plot(times, data, linestyle=(i, (i+1, i+2)), linewidth=2, label=i)
      
  plt.xlabel("Time (s)")
  plt.ylabel("unit like radian, meter, or Newton")
  plt.title(title)
  plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
  plt.legend()
  plt.tight_layout()
  plt.show()  

print(control_outputs)

print("The iiwa arm has seven joints.")
PlotState("iiwa.position", control_logs)

print("The gripper has one commanded postion: opening width.")
